note: Intent -> the path to take, the alternatives, and the one anchor to open. Hand-authored and gated by knowledge/tools/routing/check-routes.mjs. Prose stays in docs/: a route ends the choice, it does not restate the guide.

tasks.intent: Put two columns of content side by side on the page.
tasks.recommendedBecause: docs/recipes/layered-page-design.md#sidebar-page-background-vs-row states it directly: a column that holds content is a row column, because it flows and paginates with the main column.

alternatives.useWhen: the column is a tint that must repeat on every page and holds no content
alternatives.tradeoffs: costs nothing at layout time and never shifts content, but nothing can be placed in it — text in the sidebar still needs a row over the tint

alternatives.useWhen: the two columns are a data grid with a header row, not a page region
alternatives.tradeoffs: paginates per row and sizes columns by table rules rather than weights; a skills list in two columns is a row, not a table

alternatives.useWhen: the region is a fixed box needing pixel-precise (x, y) placement — a certificate or a badge
alternatives.tradeoffs: no flow and no pagination at all; the coordinates are yours to maintain

tasks.intent: Decide which of the four placement tools a piece of page design needs.
tasks.recommendedBecause: docs/recipes/layered-page-design.md#the-four-tools presents flow as the default and the other three as the cases where flow is not enough.

alternatives.useWhen: the thing is a surface that repeats on every page and holds no content
alternatives.tradeoffs: free at layout time; cannot contain anything

alternatives.useWhen: elements genuinely overlap and the overlay should size itself to what it sits on
alternatives.tradeoffs: measures and sizes with its parent, so it stays correct when content changes

alternatives.useWhen: placement is pixel-precise inside a fixed box and must not reflow
alternatives.tradeoffs: no flow, no pagination, no measurement — coordinates are maintained by hand

tasks.intent: Keep a table's header row visible when the table runs past a page break.
tasks.recommendedBecause: docs/recipes/tables.md#repeated-header-on-page-break documents repeatHeader() for exactly this, and TableBuilderRepeatHeaderTest walks every page of a 60-row table asserting it.

alternatives.useWhen: each page's rows are a distinct group the reader should not read as one run
alternatives.tradeoffs: page breaks become content decisions and stop following the data; totals must be recomputed per part
